1.explanation: All three files render the markup for the Toggle (and ToggleSmall) components and explicitly apply aria-hidden="true" to the text spans for the off/on labels. That attribute is what’s preventing VoiceOver from announcing the status text. To restore screen-reader announcement of the labels, those aria-hidden attributes need to be removed or moved only to decorative elements. Therefore these source files are the ones that must be edited to fix the bug.
1.bug_scenario: When tabbing to and toggling the default Toggle component with VoiceOver on macOS, the On/Off text labels aren’t announced because both spans carrying “Off” and “On” have aria-hidden="true" applied. VoiceOver skips over any element marked aria-hidden, so the user only hears “checkbox checked” without contextual label.

2.explanation:
All of these files are responsible for rendering the Toggle component (React and vanilla):

• packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle.js
  - This is the React implementation of the Toggle. Recent changes added aria-hidden on the label spans here, preventing screen readers from reading the On/Off text.

• packages/react/src/components/Toggle/ToggleSmall.js
  - The small-variant toggle shares the same span structure and was also updated with aria-hidden, so it will exhibit the same issue.

• packages/components/src/components/toggle/toggle.js
  - This is the vanilla Web component source for Toggle. It likewise injects aria-hidden on the text spans, hiding them from VoiceOver.

• packages/components/src/components/toggle/toggle.config.js
  - The configuration file controls how the vanilla component is templated. It includes the markup for the left/right text spans, and will need to be updated to remove aria-hidden so that screen readers can access the label text.
2.bug_scenario: When navigating to the default Toggle component with VoiceOver on macOS and activating it via keyboard, the screen reader does not announce the “On” or “Off” labels.  In the DOM you can see that both label spans (<span class="bx--toggle__text--left"> and <span class="bx--toggle__text--right">) carry aria-hidden="true", which hides the text from assistive technology.  If you remove aria-hidden the labels are announced correctly.
